prompt:
Design brief — your own take on this character. A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of Meng Huo from the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, reimagined as an adult woman — the Nanman king captured seven times and released seven times. Age: late twenties — a graceful grown-up face with soft, smooth contours; no wrinkles, folds or under-eye bags. She is a woman — no beard, moustache or facial hair.

You design her yourself: invent her face, eye colour, hairstyle, makeup, expression, pose and setting as a fresh, original take — do not follow any earlier design of this character. Her hair colour, skin tone, costume and weapon are NOT free: take them from our designs below.

Style (fixed): Premium Korean MMORPG promotional character render: a semi-realistic, painterly 3D finish with porcelain skin and a soft subsurface glow, a small refined face with delicate realistic-anime features, long legs and a narrow waist on a full, curvaceous figure with soft volume at bust, hips and thighs. Glossy specular highlights on skin, fabric and jewellery. Refined fabric and accessory rendering with fine jewellery detail. Ethereal rim lighting, drifting light particles and atmospheric depth with a softly blurred background. Luxurious, high-detail, character-select-screen quality.

Inspiration only: proud stubbornness and final loyalty, beast-tooth necklace, tribal gold.

World (fixed): the chaos of the late Eastern Han, around 184–200 AD: burning Luoyang, the Hulao Pass, Yellow Turban fields, warlord camps of rival banners, frontier steppe and the southern jungles of the Nanman. Her costume, weapon and setting belong to this world.

Costume (choose one of ours, then add your own idea): pick ONE of these costume shapes from our set and keep its overall silhouette — 1) light armor pieces over a fitted silk martial dress, long silk sashes and a light skirt flowing from the waist and shoulders — a light, dancing silhouette; 2) layered laced lamellar armor, big heavy beast-head pauldrons and armored skirts to the knees — a broad, weighty general's silhouette; 3) fitted light lamellar armor with short armored skirts slit for riding, bracers and greaves — a lean, practical cavalry silhouette; 4) a fitted martial-arts outfit with a wide belt and arm guards, a long silk sash streaming behind — a wandering swordswoman's silhouette; 5) a great war cape spreading from the shoulders to the ankles as the main shape, lamellar armor beneath; 6) a heavy fur mantle over the shoulders with leather straps and beast ornaments — a rugged frontier silhouette; 7) a lamellar breastplate above, many layers of silk skirt flaring wide below the waist — firm above, flowing below; 8) a dark close-fitting light outfit with minimal ornament and wrapped arms and legs — a sleek silhouette, face uncovered; 9) a chest guard, a quiver, a fitted short robe and leg wraps — a light, upright archer's silhouette. Then add one signature idea of your own drawn from her legend, built into the construction of the outfit itself rather than as a print or a loose accessory — e.g. plates or cloth layered like feathers, scales or petals, a hem or sleeve cut into a motif from her story. Build it in this world's materials and our colours below.

Weapon (fixed — ours): a great southern broadsword.

Hair colour (fixed — ours): deep indigo hair. Keep exactly this hair colour; only the hairstyle is yours.

Skin tone (fixed — ours): bronze-brown skin. Keep exactly this skin tone.

Costume colours (ours): bronze-gold, deep crimson, jade green and dark wood brown.

Rank (fixed): she is a famed war general — her costume must read battlefield might at first glance: imposing, richly worked armour and cloth with flagship-card detail, never plain or sparse.

Exposure (fixed): bold — her outfit shows skin by design (a deep neckline, bare shoulders or arms, a high slit or short hem); intimate areas covered.

Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin — never a long face or a long, pointed or heavy jaw; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline and never lengthens her face. Her eyes stay at a natural open size — never squeezed into narrow slits.

Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her crown or headpiece to both boots stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every genre; her hands and her signature item stay inside the frame. Camera at chest height with natural portrait perspective — no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

If you have already drawn a free design of her in this session, make this one clearly different — another face and hairstyle (the same hair colour and skin tone), another costume shape from the list with another signature idea, another pose and setting.

Write your own detailed image prompt from this brief, then draw it. One figure only, natural hands with five fingers; a banner or seal may carry a single faction character, no other text; no logo or watermark.
